claim: The gaseous plant hormone ethylene regulates a multitude of growth and developmental processes.
source_text: The gaseous plant hormone ethylene regulates a multitude of growth and developmental processes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established fact in plant biology that represents general scientific consensus about ethylene's role.

claim: EIN3 is the master regulator of the ethylene signaling pathway.
source_text: identifying targets of the master regulator of the ethylene signaling pathway, ETHYLENE INSENSITIVE3 (EIN3)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by prior research and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Ethylene-induced transcription occurs in temporal waves regulated by EIN3.
source_text: Ethylene-induced transcription occurs in temporal waves regulated by EIN3, suggesting distinct layers of transcriptional control.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq experimental data presented in the manuscript showing temporal patterns of transcription.

claim: EIN3 binding modulates a major feedback regulatory circuitry of the ethylene signaling pathway.

claim: An EIN3-dependent sustained growth inhibition follows the rapid growth inhibition in response to ethylene.
source_text: followed by an EIN3-dependent sustained growth inhibition
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Binder et al., 2004a.

claim: EIN3 accumulates upon a duration of exogenous ethylene gas treatment.
source_text: EIN3 has been shown to be necessary and sufficient for the ethylene response and accumulates upon a duration of exogenous ethylene gas treatment
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Guo and Ecker, 2003.

claim: EIN3 is necessary and sufficient for the ethylene response.
source_text: EIN3 has been shown to be necessary and sufficient for the ethylene response
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Guo and Ecker, 2003.

claim: Hundreds of ethylene response genes have been identified.
source_text: Although hundreds of ethylene response genes have been identified

claim: EIN3 activates a transcriptional cascade.

claim: Transcription factor binding does not necessarily coincide with changes in transcription.

source_text: The four waves of ethylene-induced transcription account for 50% of the transcriptionally ethylene-regulated EIN3 targets (EIN3-R)

claim: During sustained exogenous ethylene application, EIN3 accumulates, and the established ethylene transcriptional response is hormone-focused and less noisy.

claim: Hormones operate in concert, synergistically/antagonistically regulating growth and development.
source_text: because hormones operate in concert, synergistically/antagonistically regulating growth and development
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge in plant biology.

source_text: Although hormone pathway interconnections have been previously described by many groups

claim: Several negative regulators of the ethylene signaling pathway are targets of EIN3, including ETR2, ERS1/2, RTE1, CTR1, and EBF1/2.
source_text: More specifically, several negative regulators of the ethylene signaling pathway (Kendrick and Chang, 2008) were targets of EIN3 (Figure 3A), including three ethylene receptors (ETHYLENE RESPONSE2 [ETR2], ETHYLENE RESPONSE SENSOR1/2 [ERS1/2]), as well as REVERSION-TO-ETHYLENE SENSITIVITY1 (RTE1), CONSTITUTIVE TRIPLE RESPONSE1 (CTR1), and the previously mentioned EBF1/2.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the ChIP-Seq data identifying these genes as EIN3 targets.

claim: The induction of ETR2, ERS1/2 by ethylene was previously reported and has been suggested to restore ethylene receptor activity, resensitizing the plant to ethylene.
source_text: The induction of ETR2, ERS1/2 by ethylene was previously reported and has been suggested to restore ethylene receptor activity, resensitizing the plant to ethylene
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Binder et al., 2004b and Vandenbussche et al., 2012.

claim: The negative regulation of ethylene signaling by EIN3 through induction of CTR1 and ETR2 is supported by literature showing these proteins exhibit increased stabilization upon ethylene treatment.
source_text: The negative regulation of ethylene signaling by EIN3 through induction of CTR1 and ETR2 is further supported by the literature (Chen et al., 2007), suggesting that these proteins exhibit an increase in stabilization upon ethylene treatment
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2007 and Gao et al., 2003.

claim: EIN3 candidate targets account for more than twice the proportion of hormone genes than in the genome (46%).
source_text: The EIN3 candidate targets account for more than twice the proportion of hormone genes than in the genome (46%, Hypergeometric p=10−96)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis comparing EIN3 targets to the genome.

claim: Many genes involved in hormone response are involved in more than one hormone response, highlighting extensive hormone co-regulation in Arabidopsis.
source_text: Many of the genes were involved in more than one hormone response, highlighting the extensive hormone co-regulation in Arabidopsis
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the hormone annotation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Hormone co-regulation is evident in protein-protein as well as transcriptional regulator interactions.
source_text: Hormone co-regulation is evident in the protein-protein as well as the transcriptional regulator interactions and this network reveals interconnectivity suggestive of robust regulatory co-regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the network analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Hormone co-regulation can occur through the binding of EIN3.
source_text: The findings presented in our study suggest that (1) hormone co-regulation can occur through the binding of EIN3

claim: EIN3 targets hormone pathways at multiple levels.
source_text: (2) EIN3 targets hormone pathways at multiple levels

claim: Some EIN3-mediated hormone co-regulation events are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene.
source_text: and (3) some of these events are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene

claim: Ethylene and jasmonate co-regulation occurs at the transcriptional level, sharing a complement of genes responsive to both hormones, including RAP2.6L and ERF1.
source_text: Ethylene and jasmonate co-regulation occurs at the transcriptional level, sharing a complement of genes responsive to both hormones, for example RAP2.6L, ERF1.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis of EIN3 targets and their hormone annotations.

claim: EIN3 targets four JAZ repressors, two of which are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (JAZ1, JAZ6).
source_text: EIN3 also targets four JAZ repressors, two of which are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (JAZ1, JAZ6).

claim: In the presence of jasmonate, JAZ1 proteins bound to EIN3 are degraded, relieving EIN3 transcriptional activation.
source_text: In general, ethylene and jasmonate are known to function synergistically and in the presence of jasmonate, JAZ1 proteins bound to EIN3 are degraded, relieving the EIN3 transcriptional activation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2011.

claim: The presence of exogenous ethylene stimulus primes cells for a jasmonate response by loading promoters of jasmonate/ethylene response genes with EIN3 and JAZ proteins.
source_text: Here, the presence of an exogenous ethylene stimulus primes cells for a jasmonate response, by loading the promoters of jasmonate/ethylene response genes with EIN3 and JAZ proteins, poising the plant for a jasmonate-ethylene driven transcriptional program, as required for plant pathogen response.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the ChIP-Seq data showing EIN3 binding to jasmonate pathway genes.

claim: Anticipatory binding has been reported in other organisms.
source_text: Reports of anticipatory binding in other organisms have been forth coming
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Macquarrie et al., 2011 and Lickwar et al., 2012.

claim: Ethylene and gibberellin co-regulation through EIN3 occurs at signal reception (GID1B, GID1C) and transcription (PIF3).
source_text: Ethylene and gibberellin co-regulation through EIN3 occurs at signal reception (GID1B, GID1C) and transcription (PIF3).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the ChIP-Seq data showing EIN3 binding to these genes.

claim: The regulatory logic of EIN3 binding results in an up-regulation of the gibberellin response through GID receptors targeting DELLA repressors for degradation, which releases PIF3 from repression.
source_text: The regulatory logic of EIN3 binding results in an up-regulation of the gibberellin response; GID receptors target DELLA repressors for degradation, which releases PIF3 from repression, resulting in the activation of the gibberellin transcriptional response.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the ChIP-Seq data combined with established knowledge of gibberellin signaling.

claim: The PIF3 motif is over-represented in the promoter sequences of ethylene transcriptional response genes.
source_text: Additional support for feed-forward transcription is provided by over-representation of the PIF3 motif in the promoter sequences of the ethylene transcriptional response genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the motif enrichment analysis shown in Supplementary file 1E.

claim: FUSCA3 negatively regulates ethylene by targeting genes upstream and downstream of EIN3 (EIN2 and ERF1) in leaf aging.
source_text: Hormone co-regulation may also occur bidirectionally as a recent study reported negative regulation of ethylene by FUSCA3 (FUS3), known to regulate and be regulated by gibberellin and abscisic acid in embryonic and vegetative timing (Lumba et al., 2012). FUS3 negatively regulates genes upstream and downstream of EIN3 (EIN2 and ERF1) in leaf aging

claim: Ethylene and auxin co-regulation occurs at both the level of transport and transcriptional response.

claim: EIN3 targets the auxin transporter AUX1 and auxin signaling gene IAA29, but these are not responsive to ethylene in etiolated seedlings.
source_text: EIN3 also targets the auxin transporter (AUX1) and an auxin signaling gene (IAA29), but these candidate targets are not responsive to ethylene in etiolated seedlings

claim: Ethylene stimulates auxin transport through AUX1 away from the root apex to decrease lateral root primordia.

claim: EIN3 targets that may regulate a secondary transcriptional ethylene response include AT-ERF1, ERF5, WRKY14/47, PIF3, NAC6, and RAP2.2.
source_text: EIN3 targets that may regulate a secondary transcriptional ethylene response include AP2/ERFs AT-ERF1, ERF5, and WRKY14/47, PIF3, NAC6, and RAP2.2
